question.text: Patanjali Herbals Fund (Cat II): INR 120 crore committed and called. Hurdle 9% compounded. Fund tenure 4 years. Compute the cumulative PREFERRED RETURN at end of Year 4 (return accruing solely to investors before any GP carry).

explanation.text: The Logic: Hurdle NAV Year 4 = INR 120 x (1.09)^4 = INR 120 x 1.41158 = INR 169.39 crore. Preferred return = 169.39 - 120 = INR 49.39 crore (≈ INR 49.38 cr), matching keyed option D. Workbook p.119 is explicit that closed-ended Cat I/II hurdle NAV is compounded, not simple. The Trap: A is simple interest 9% x 4 x 120 = INR 43.20 cr (wrong — compound, not simple); B is the gross 9% x 4 x 120 / 1.2 framing without compounding; C is the 5-year compound figure (~INR 50.57 cr). Option D is the keyed correct answer. Note: Corrected the trap label that previously described option D as a 2-year calculation; D is the keyed correct answer. Removed the reporting-transparency pro-tip and the Cross-Exam Context paragraph, since both go beyond the source's compound-hurdle support on p.119.
